source.title: Reasoning over Precedents Alongside Statutes: Case-Augmented Deliberative Alignment for LLM Safety
source.authors: Can Jin; Rui Wu; Tong Che; Qi-Xin Zhang; Hong-Wu Peng; Jia-Hui Zhao; Zhen-Ting Wang; Wen-Qi Wei; Ligong Han; Zhao Zhang; Yuan Cao; Rui-Xiang Tang; Dimitris N. Metaxas

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how safety-oriented training on harmful requests and jailbreak attacks affect harmful-request compliance, using different training objectives and evaluation measures from the claim’s cited studies.
record.gate_note: Reports harmful-request ASR after safety training on harmful prompts, and ASR under PAIR and PAP attacks. The fine-tuning targets refusals or safety reasoning, not harmful completions, so it does not reproduce the harmful-compliance-target fine-tuning described in V1. It does not measure token-position KL, compliant-opening prefills, decoding changes, localized parameters, or training intended to deepen token-level safety.
record.test_reason: This is a safety-alignment method paper (CADA). It trains models toward refusal or safety reasoning on harmful requests and reports its own method's ASR against baselines. No version is tested. There is no fine-tuning on harmful-compliance or benign data (V1, V2), no per-token KL (V3), and no prefill, suffix or decoding attack (V4; PAIR and PAP are prompt-rewriting jailbreaks). It has no localization (V5), no shallowness mechanism (V6), and no training meant to spread safety past the first tokens (V7). Qi et al. is cited only as the HEx-PHI benchmark.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that case-augmented reasoning beats extensive code-like rules. At inference time, explicit codes inconsistently help harmlessness and degrade helpfulness. CADA, RL on self-generated case-augmented reasoning, improves harmlessness, jailbreak robustness and over-refusal without hurting utility, using a few hundred samples.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares refusal-target SFT, safety-reasoning SFT, DPO, and CADA reinforcement learning on harmful requests. It does not apply the original harmful-compliance fine-tuning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model, training method, benchmark, and attack: PAIR and PAP ASRs differ, and CADA’s ASR reductions versus w/o SR are larger in some model/benchmark settings than others.

fits_no_version.finding: Prompt-level jailbreaks still succeed after refusal or safety-reasoning training on about 500 harmful requests. Deepthought-8B PAIR ASR stays at 76–85% after CADA, versus 84–93% untrained. Refusal-only SFT lowers Deepthought PAP ASR to 6.07, versus 31–40 for reasoning SFT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety SFT or RL on a few hundred harmful requests only partly reduces semantic-jailbreak (PAIR/PAP) success, and reasoning models stay highly vulnerable.

fits_no_version.finding: Non-refusal on XSTest safe requests after safety training on harmful requests.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Case-augmented SFT, DPO or CADA changes over-refusal, with direction depending on method.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: Only two models are used for the main training experiments. The paper evaluates two named jailbreak attacks and notes that it cannot guarantee immunity to unseen attacks. Table 2 reports no uncertainty values; reported results are averaged over three runs in the later experiments.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 SFT w CR and DPO w CR ASR rows are omitted; Table 2 already records the safety-training comparison and Table 3 CADA rows capture the reported CADA attack outcomes. Other Table 4 utility metrics (GSM8K, BBH, MMLU) are omitted because they do not measure the claim’s specified behavior.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on harmful-compliance examples; all training targets refusal or safety reasoning.
No prefill, adversarial suffix or decoding attack; only PAIR and PAP prompt jailbreaks.
CADA is reasoning-based RL, not token-depth augmentation, and depth is not measured.

record.verdict_notes: The reader mislinked all Table 2/3 ASR rows to V1 and V4. Several PAP and attack-control rows have the attack value copied as the no-attack baseline. Table 1 (inference-time safety codes raise LLaMA PAIR ASR from 44.41 to 78.27) is not recorded, but it bears on no version either.

versions.untested_parts: The study trains on harmful requests paired with refusals or safety reasoning, not harmful-compliance examples; it does not reproduce fine-tuning a safety-trained checkpoint on examples that teach harmful compliance.
No benign instruction data is used for fine-tuning to test whether it raises harmful compliance.
No per-response-position KL divergence or aligned-versus-base output-distribution comparison is reported.
Tests PAIR and PAP jailbreak attacks, but not compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes specifically, or decoding changes.
No weight or rank localization experiment is reported.
Does not test whether data or training objectives produce first-token shallowness.
Does not train or measure safety distributed beyond initial response tokens.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Safety-target training on harmful requests, without attacks
reader_labels.reason: The intervention trains refusals or safety reasoning, not harmful compliance; most reported ASRs are lower than w/o SR, so the result does not establish that harmful-compliance-target examples produce the claimed effect (rows t2-l8-dr-none, t2-l8-cr-none, t2-dt-dr-none, t2-dt-sc-none, t2-dt-cr-none).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: PAIR and PAP attacks in the tested benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: The attacks yield nonzero ASR in multiple model and training conditions, showing some harmful compliance under jailbreak attacks (rows t2-l8-dr-pair, t2-l8-sc-pair, t2-l8-cr-pair, t2-dt-dr-pair, t2-dt-sc-pair, t2-dt-cr-pair, t3-l8-cada-sr-pair, t3-l8-cada-sr-pap, t3-dt-cada-sr-pair, t3-dt-cada-sr-pap).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Attack outcomes across training methods and models
reader_labels.reason: Attack success varies substantially; CADA lowers ASR versus w/o SR, and the PAP results for LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct after SFT match the no-attack values (rows t2-l8-dr-pap, t2-l8-sc-pap, t2-l8-cr-pap, t3-l8-cada-sr-pair, t3-dt-cada-sr-pair).
